title: Mexican Crime Photographs from the Archive of Stefan Ruiz

description.main: Mexican Crime Photographs from the Archive of Stefan Ruiz (GOST Books, 2015) publishes over 100 mugshots, robbery stills and drawn portraits of suspects and stolen jewels from Mexico City, late 1950s to early 1970s, with an essay by Benjamin Smith. 187 pages, clothbound.
description.extended:
Stefan Ruiz's Mexican Crime Photographs publishes a found police-style archive from Mexico City: over 100 mugshots, robbery stills and drawn portraits of criminals and stolen jewelry from the late 1950s to the early 1970s.

In 2010 Ruiz came across the photographs on a stall at La Lagunilla, the thrift market in Mexico City. Over six months he met the seller repeatedly and bought more of the collection each time. Many of the images are damaged, some are kept in their original groups, and all carry handwritten annotations in white. Ruiz never learned the source, though the photographs probably come from the city's police archives. The book adds an essay by Benjamin Smith, a historian of Latin America at the University of Warwick, who reads the material against the return of the PRI in 2012 and Mexico's continuing news of crime, police corruption and impunity. It is a 187-page clothbound hardback, 160 × 120 mm, published by GOST Books in November 2015.

Ruiz is a Berlin-based photographer. His book San Francisco Berlin (Boot, 2011) is also in the library.

notes: Published November 2015. Essay by Dr Benjamin Smith, Associate Professor of Latin American History, University of Warwick.
